name: Boundary Dam Unit 3 CCS
description: World's first commercial-scale post-combustion CCS retrofit on a coal-fired power unit (110 MW lignite), operating since 2014. It has captured CO₂ well below its ~1 Mtpa design target, with frequent outages and low availability.

name: Quest CCS
description: Shell-operated amine CCS capturing CO₂ from three hydrogen manufacturing units at the Scotford Upgrader since 2015, stored ~2 km underground in the Basal Cambrian Sands. It has exceeded its ~1 Mtpa target, storing over 7 million tonnes cumulatively.

name: Nutrien Redwater CCS
description: Captures CO₂ from ammonia and hydrogen production at Nutrien's Redwater nitrogen complex and exports it into the Alberta Carbon Trunk Line. A 2023 expansion raised capture/export capacity to over 300,000 t/yr.

name: North West Redwater Sturgeon Refinery CCS
operator: North West Redwater Partnership (Canadian Natural Resources / Alberta Government)
description: Gasification-based bitumen refinery that produces a pure, dry CO₂ stream captured rather than vented, serving as the anchor supply for the Alberta Carbon Trunk Line. Captures up to ~1.2 Mtpa of CO₂.

name: Alberta Carbon Trunk Line (ACTL)
description: 240 km CO₂ pipeline network linking Redwater-area emitters to enhanced oil recovery and permanent geological storage in central Alberta, operating since 2020. Its large design capacity of ~14.6 Mtpa is far above actual utilisation.

name: Glacier Gas Plant CCS
description: Entropy's modular post-combustion CCS at Advantage Energy's Glacier gas plant, capturing from compression engines since 2022 and expanded in 2026 with a 15 MW cogeneration unit integrated with capture. Captures ~192,000 t/yr.

name: Shell Polaris CCS
description: Second CCS unit at Shell's Scotford Energy and Chemicals Park, with FID taken June 2024 to capture ~650,000 t/yr of CO₂ from refinery and upgrader operations. Expected to start up toward the end of 2028.

name: Shell Atlas Carbon Storage Hub
description: CO₂ storage hub developed by Shell in partnership with ATCO EnPower near Scotford, with FID taken June 2024. Phase 1 will provide permanent storage for CO₂ captured by the Polaris project, with capacity to expand for third-party emitters.

name: Air Products Edmonton Net-Zero Hydrogen Complex
description: Net-zero hydrogen production complex in northeast Edmonton supplying blue hydrogen to Imperial Oil's Strathcona refinery, with autothermal reforming and carbon capture of roughly 1 Mtpa CO₂ for transport and storage. Construction is well underway.

name: Enhance Energy Origins CCS Hub
description: Open-access carbon capture and storage hub near Clive, Alberta, set to become Canada's largest operating sequestration facility. Broke ground in 2026 with commercial operations targeted for January 2027 and built-in expansion capacity.

name: Pathways Alliance CCS Hub
operator: Pathways Alliance (Cenovus, Suncor, Canadian Natural, Imperial, ConocoPhillips, MEG Energy)
description: Proposed oil-sands CCS network connecting ~20 facilities across the Fort McMurray and Cold Lake regions to a shared storage hub. Estimated at ~$16.5B and targeting ~10–12 Mtpa, it remains pre-FID with a decision targeted for late 2027.

name: Dow Fort Saskatchewan Path2Zero
description: Dow's world-first net-zero Scope 1 and 2 ethylene cracker and derivatives expansion, with carbon capture and storage reducing existing emissions by ~1 Mtpa and abating all new capacity emissions. FID taken November 2023, later delayed and reaffirmed with a 2029–2030 start-up timeline.

name: Linde Fort Saskatchewan Clean Hydrogen
description: Linde's ~$2B blue hydrogen complex at Fort Saskatchewan, using autothermal reforming with carbon capture to supply clean hydrogen to Dow's Path2Zero site. FID taken; supports the net-zero ethylene complex.

name: Heidelberg Materials Edmonton CCUS
description: Heidelberg Materials' ~1 Mtpa cement CCUS project at its Edmonton plant, sending captured CO₂ by pipeline to the Wabamun Carbon Hub. Originally slated for late 2026, it was placed on hold in 2026 amid weak carbon pricing and regulatory uncertainty.

name: Lafarge Exshaw Cement CCS
description: Lafarge Canada's carbon capture development at its Exshaw cement plant in the Bow Valley, at pre-FID feasibility/pilot stage. Part of broader efforts to decarbonise Alberta cement production.

name: Open Access Wabamun Carbon Hub
description: Enbridge's open-access CO₂ transportation and storage hub near Wabamun, serving multiple Edmonton-region emitters including Heidelberg Materials. Approved by the Alberta government; Phase 1 targets ~1 Mtpa with expansion potential.

name: Alberta Carbon Grid
description: TC Energy and Pembina Pipeline's proposed open-access CO₂ transportation and storage hub across Alberta's industrial heartland. In early development.
